name: Dynamite and Discovery: The Nobel Prizes in Science
description: One inventor's will created the world's best-known prizes. Follow the laureates in physics, chemistry and medicine and the discoveries that earned them.

checkpoints.name: The will and the first prizes
checkpoints.note: Alfred Nobel died in 1896 and left his fortune for prizes. The first physics prize went to Rontgen in 1901, and the Curies and Becquerel won in 1903. Thomson and Rutherford were soon honoured, while Planck's quantum and Haber's ammonia process won prizes later, in 1918.

checkpoints.name: The quantum years
checkpoints.note: Einstein won for the photoelectric effect and Bohr for the atom's structure. Schrodinger, Dirac and Heisenberg built quantum mechanics, and the medicine prize honoured insulin.

checkpoints.name: War and after
checkpoints.note: Chadwick's neutron and Fermi's neutron work were rewarded, as were Fleming's penicillin and the later chemistry of vitamins. Chandrasekhar's work on dying stars would be honoured later.

checkpoints.name: Molecules of life
checkpoints.note: Hodgkin, and Watson, Crick and Wilkins for DNA, opened up biological structure. McClintock won for jumping genes, Levi-Montalcini for nerve growth, Feynman for quantum electrodynamics, and Borlaug the Peace Prize for crop breeding.

checkpoints.name: A new century
checkpoints.note: Tu Youyou won for artemisinin against malaria, Doudna and Charpentier for CRISPR gene editing, Englert and Higgs for predicting the Higgs boson, and three LIGO leaders for gravitational waves. These discoveries rested on huge teams, but no more than three people can share a prize.
